sense: belonging to a particular art, trade or science

evidence: Cic. N.D. 2.57: Zēnō cēnset artis proprium esse creāre et gignere (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin says what belongs to an art with the genitive artis or the name of the field: a technical term is vocābulum artis proprium, or one of the field (mīlitāre vocābulum, Tac. Ann. 1.41). The phrase is ours, made after Cicero’s artis proprium.

terms.gloss: according to the rules of an art
terms.comment: Only in Quintilian (Lewis & Short), of the proofs the orator makes by his art, as against those he finds.

terms.gloss: a teacher of an art (not an adjective)
terms.comment: In Latin a noun, “a teacher of an art” (Lewis & Short), Quintilian’s word for the writers on the art of rhetoric; it does not mean “technical”.

phrases.english: whom they called Caligula, in the soldiers’ word

sources: Lewis & Short: proprius · Lewis & Short: artificialis · Lewis & Short: technicus
